criteria.claim: Recovery reconstructs readable in-memory state from a temporary/local WAL handle but finishes without installing/reopening the member wal_file_.
criteria.full_credit: Name the local-versus-member distinction and show replay enters internal operations that populate memory/doc ids. A generic claim of stale cache is insufficient.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for correct recovered-memory state or correct local/member WAL distinction, but not both.

criteria.claim: flush() treats a null member WAL or one with no records as no pending work, returning OK before persistence. Here the null member arm triggers.
criteria.full_credit: State the exact null-or-no-record guard, identify the null-member cause for this scenario, and explain the skipped persistence/finalization.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for identifying flush as the skipped step without the precise condition or lifecycle consequences.

criteria.claim: Optimize -> switch_to_new_segment_for_writing -> dump -> flush; successful early return allows sealing/switching and version persistence after old writing-block metadata is removed, so a future open cannot recover/persist the lost memory via the old writing block.
criteria.full_credit: Connect the full call chain to removal of old writing metadata and the new persisted version, rather than blaming vector-ranking quality or claiming optimize never calls flush.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for correct call chain without the metadata/reopen consequence, or correct consequence without the chain.

criteria.claim: Same-handle Stats reads in-memory segment counts and indexed metadata; success/index completeness is not a durability or data-content check.
criteria.full_credit: Explain doc_ids_ based counting and metadata-derived index completeness; do not invent a separate stats cache.

criteria.claim: Normal Insert appends to/opens the member WAL before internal_insert, unlike replay, explaining the no-crash control under the stated size assumptions.
criteria.full_credit: Cite ordinary insertion and append/open behavior; distinguish recovery bypassing append_wal.

criteria.claim: Restore the invariant that replayed pending data has an attached usable member WAL before later flush/dump; close the temporary reader and reopen/retain the existing WAL through the normal member path, handling errors.
criteria.full_credit: A minimal lifecycle repair equivalent to attaching/reopening the existing WAL is accepted. An alternative persistence design is accepted only if the answer proves it preserves version, flush and WAL cleanup invariants.
criteria.partial_credit: No partial point; simply calling public flush on the broken state is not a repair.

criteria.claim: Regression: insert known documents, force abrupt termination before flush, reopen and verify recovered data, optimize without extra writes, close, reopen from fresh process and compare count plus representative/all known documents and vectors. Include a no-crash or already-flushed control.
criteria.full_credit: Fresh reopen after optimize and no intervening writes are required, because same-handle checks and writes that lazily open the WAL can mask the defect. Executing the test is not required.
